meta.title: Ranked decision analysis — best choice to inquire with first
meta.nature: Editorial priority order for inquiry, not an official rating, verified performance score, quotation or booking. No numeric score is assigned because no official source ranks contractors for this repair.
meta.method: Order the officially verified licence facts first (active C-36 plumbing; lawful combined-trade structure), then the strongest published adjacent case evidence, then occupied-unit/service evidence, then existing owner-supplied quote scope. Downgrade adverse CSLB status, unresolved identity, insurance expiry, and out-of-scope or ambiguous quotes. Values that cannot be confirmed from an official source are blank and flagged.
meta.verification: Every licence, classification, status, expiry and business phone below was re-read on the official CSLB licence-detail page on 2026-11-08. Company-site statements are labelled self-descriptions. Amounts attributed to the owner are labelled unverified; verified amounts remain blank.

criteria.criterion: Active C-36 plumbing licence on the checked CSLB record
criteria.why: The plumbing leg includes waste/overflow piping; C-36 is the official classification that covers removal of waste, piping, maintenance and replacement.
criteria.limit: A classification is a legal scope, not proof that the firm accepts this exact delicate job.

criteria.criterion: Lawful single-contract capacity for plumbing plus drywall/restoration
criteria.why: BPC §7057 allows a B prime contract involving two unrelated trades, or the appropriate specialty class/subcontractor. B + C-36 on one licence, or a named C-9/B restoration partner, fits the requested all-in-one service.
criteria.limit: B + C-36 is not proof that the firm self-performs drywall texture and paint; the contract must name the party.

criteria.criterion: Published adjacent ceiling-access tub waste/overflow case
criteria.why: A documented below-ceiling tub waste/overflow replacement is the closest public evidence to the fallback access route described in the brief.
criteria.limit: Company-published case text is self-reported, not an independent review; the page also embeds a 404 template block (F-17).

criteria.criterion: San Francisco service area and occupied-unit coordination evidence
criteria.why: The unit is tenant-occupied and the access is in a storage area below; service-area and occupied-space statements matter for a delicate, coordinated visit.
criteria.limit: Company self-descriptions are not confirmations of availability, insurance or a current written protocol.

criteria.why: Three firms have already quoted scopes, which lowers outreach effort, but only one scope wording resembles a full waste-and-overflow replacement.
criteria.limit: All three amounts are owner-reported and unverified; the scopes differ and none explicitly prices ceiling restoration.

criteria.criterion: Adverse CSLB status, unresolved identity or expiring insurance
criteria.why: Suspension, an additional-status warning, a complaint-disclosure record, an unresolved licence match or an insurance expiry raises signing-day risk.
criteria.limit: CSLB status is point-in-time; re-check the linked page before signing.

criteria.why: Official DBI fees are verified; contractor prices are not. A permit fee is not a repair quote and cannot be added to a quote until inclusions and the DBI category are confirmed.
criteria.limit: Job-specific permit applicability and the drywall restoration price remain unconfirmed; those cells are blank.

ranks.reason: Best structural fit for an all-in-one prime contract: one active licence holds both B and C-36, which satisfies the two-unrelated-trades rule for plumbing plus restoration. Its official site self-describes general contracting and simple repairs to renovations. Ranked first on licence structure, not on verified performance.
ranks.cost: No current written quote on file; the verified price cell is blank. Owner-reported amounts of $614, $550 and $135 belong to three other firms with unlike scopes and are unverified, so they are not a comparable price. Official DBI Category 1P is $290 if that category and a permit apply; off-hour inspection is $555/hour. Ask for one itemized combined quote.
ranks.unverified: Exact stuck-lever job acceptance, named drywall/texture/paint party, occupied-unit plan, current price, and which published phone number dispatches work (F-37).

ranks.reason: Second-strongest structural fit: active B + C-36 plus the broadest classification set in the register, licensed since 2003. Its official site self-describes long-running work with HOAs and property managers, relevant to an occupied unit. Ranked below Rapid Flow because no published case of this exact access route was found and a 2007 licence reissue is recorded.
ranks.cost: No quote on file; verified price blank. The owner-reported $614/$550/$135 figures are unverified and belong to other firms. Official DBI fees ($290 Category 1P; $519/hour regular inspection; $259/half-hour reinspection) are separate from any contractor price. Request a written combined scope and price.
ranks.unverified: Acceptance of a small occupied-unit repair, named restoration party, current protocol and price; older review excerpts are not a current protocol (F-16).

ranks.reason: Strongest published technical evidence: the company's own Ingleside case describes accessing an exterior ceiling to replace a tub waste-and-overflow assembly, P-trap and trap adapter. It ranks below the B + C-36 leads because this licence has no B or C-9, so a separately named restoration contractor is required for the ceiling.
ranks.cost: No quote on file; verified price blank. The drywall opening/patch price is also blank because no official source or quote supplies it. Owner-reported amounts are unverified and from other firms. Official DBI fees are separate; a two-contractor scope needs both parties' prices in one written contract.
ranks.unverified: Restoration party, exact-job acceptance, current price and the case page's embedded 404 block (F-17); case evidence is self-published, not an independent review.

ranks.provider: Bernal Hill Drywall Inc (restoration partner, not a prime plumber)
ranks.reason: The only C-9 drywall specialist in the register and the clearest candidate to restore a ceiling opening, patch, texture and paint. Its official site self-describes small wall repairs through complete build-backs. It is ranked as the partner to name alongside a C-36 plumber, not as the sole hire for the plumbing leg.
ranks.cost: No quote on file; verified price blank. The below-ceiling drywall opening and restoration cost is blank and flagged (F-04). Owner-reported amounts and official DBI fees do not price restoration. Obtain a written restoration allowance from this or another named C-9/B firm.
ranks.unverified: Whether it accepts a small ceiling patch as a subcontractor, coordination with the plumbing prime, current price and scheduling (F-19).

ranks.reason: Active B + C-36 under one corporation with a workers'-compensation policy on file, so it has the same lawful combined-trade structure as ranks 1–2. Its official site self-describes design-build and full-gut bathroom remodels and publishes whole-project price bands, which suggests larger work; small delicate repair acceptance is unconfirmed (F-20).
ranks.cost: No quote on file; verified price blank. The site's published remodel price bands are for full remodels, not this repair, and are not used as a benchmark. Owner-reported amounts are unverified and from other firms; official DBI fees are separate. Ask whether a small repair is accepted and request an itemized quote.
ranks.unverified: Small-job acceptance, occupied-unit protocol, named restoration party and current price.

ranks.reason: Longest continuously licensed firm in the register (issued 1980) with active B + C-36 on one licence, so it can lawfully structure the combined scope. Its official site self-describes commercial design/build mechanical work, so a small tenant-occupied repair may not fit its normal project profile (F-20).
ranks.cost: No quote on file; verified price blank. No official source prices this repair. Owner-reported amounts are unverified and from other firms; official DBI fees are separate. Ask for small-repair acceptance and an itemized combined quote.
ranks.unverified: Small residential repair acceptance, occupied-unit plan, named restoration party and current price.

ranks.reason: Active B + C-36 at the same CSLB street address and business phone as Bay Area Plumbing (#757796), which quoted the owner. That combination could make one conversation cover both trades. Ranked mid-table because the CSLB records do not state who controls each licence, the firm is workers'-comp exempt (certified no employees), and its identity is not otherwise confirmed (F-12, F-28, F-30).
ranks.cost: No quote on file for this licence; verified price blank. The owner-reported $550 amount belongs to Bay Area Plumbing #757796, is unverified, and cannot be transferred to this entity. Official DBI fees are separate. Confirm the contracting entity before requesting a quote.
ranks.unverified: Legal/control relationship to #757796, who performs the work, insurance coverage, exact-job acceptance and current price.

ranks.reason: Active B + C-36 since 1974, so it has the combined-trade structure. It is ranked below the other B + C-36 firms because the official CSLB complaint-disclosure page lists a 2022 citation dated 03/23/2023 (status 'FOR DISCLOSURE ONLY PER B&P CODE 7124.6'), and the licence is workers'-comp exempt (F-11, F-28).
ranks.cost: No quote on file; verified price blank. Owner-reported amounts are unverified and from other firms; official DBI fees are separate. Review the linked disclosure and request an itemized combined quote before shortlisting.
ranks.unverified: Disclosure context, insurance for onsite workers, exact-job acceptance, named restoration party and current price.

ranks.reason: One of three firms that already supplied a quote, and its owner-reported scope ('replacing waste and overflow') is the closest wording to the full assembly that may need replacement. Ranked below combined-scope leads because C-36 alone does not cover the drywall/restoration leg, so a second licensed party is needed.
ranks.cost: Owner-reported $614 for 'replace waste and overflow' (2026-08-30), unverified; the verified amount cell is blank. The wording does not state an access route, ceiling restoration, permit, cleanup or warranty, so it is not an all-in price. Official DBI fees are separate; requote one identical combined scope.
ranks.unverified: Current validity of the supplied amount, ceiling restoration party and price, exact-job acceptance, and written scope inclusions (F-02, F-03, F-04, F-05).

ranks.reason: Existing estimate provider with an active C-36 licence since 1999. Its quoted wording ('lever for the bathtub plug and spout with diverter') may describe a different assembly than the waste-and-overflow, so the scope needs clarification. A separate B + C-36 licence (#749536) shares its CSLB address and phone, but common control is unproven (F-12).
ranks.cost: Owner-reported $550 including labour and materials (2026-08-30), unverified; verified amount blank. Because the scope may cover a tub-fill diverter rather than the waste-and-overflow, this is not comparable with the owner-reported $614 replacement or $135 adjustment. Official DBI fees are separate; requote an identical scope.
ranks.unverified: What 'spout/diverter' means, current price, contracting entity, restoration party and exact-job acceptance (F-03, F-12).

ranks.reason: Existing estimate provider with an active C-36 licence and an official site self-describing residential work with HOAs/property managers. Ranked low because the owner-reported scope is only a plunger-handle repair/adjustment (the narrowest), the CSLB workers'-compensation policy expires 2026-12-18, and the registered address wording differs from the website (F-29).
ranks.cost: Owner-reported $135 for 'repair or adjust plunger handle' (2026-08-30), unverified; verified amount blank. An adjustment-only price cannot fund a waste-and-overflow replacement plus ceiling access and restoration. Official DBI fees are separate; requote the full neutral scope and confirm insurance renewal.
ranks.unverified: Current price, insurance renewal, whether the internals can in fact be freed from above, restoration party and exact-job acceptance (F-02, F-03, F-29).

ranks.status: Current and active with CSLB additional status; expires 2027-11-30
ranks.reason: Active C-36 plumbing licence, but CSLB records an additional status: the licence may be suspended at a future date for an unresolved final liability. With no B/C-9 coverage, no quote and no published case evidence, it is the last active inquiry lead rather than a recommended first call (F-10).
ranks.cost: No quote on file; verified price blank. Owner-reported amounts are unverified and from other firms; official DBI fees are separate. Confirm licence status and obtain a written combined quote before any approach.
ranks.unverified: CSLB additional-status resolution, exact-job acceptance, restoration party and current price.

excluded.reason: CSLB shows the licence under Contractors Bond Suspension; not eligible for an inquiry lead until status is restored and a bond is verified (F-09).
No CSLB licence record could be matched to the name; licence, phone, address and status cells are blank and flagged (F-13).
Licence is B-2 Residential Remodeling, not B or C-36. BPC §7057.5 restricts contracts to three or more unrelated trades and limits plumbing-system work; not a sole prime for this job (F-08).
B-only on the checked record; its official site states it focuses on larger projects. It would need a named C-36 plumbing contractor (F-07, F-20).
A + B classifications but no C-36; a large commercial general contractor with no published evidence of small occupied-unit tub repairs (F-20).

cost_notes: The three supplied amounts ($614, $550, $135) are owner-reported primary statements dated 2026-08-30, not verified contractor prices; every verified amount cell is blank (F-02).
The scopes differ (full assembly wording, plug/lever/diverter wording, adjustment-only wording), so the $479 arithmetic spread is not a like-for-like market range (F-03).
No supplied scope explicitly prices opening and restoring the storage-unit ceiling; that cost remains blank and flagged (F-04).

Official July 2026 DBI fees are verified but are permit/inspection charges, not a repair total: Category 1P $290, Category 11P/M $320, regular inspection $519/hour, off-hour $555/hour, reinspection $259/half-hour (F-24).
Do not add a permit fee to a contractor quote until the written scope states whether permits and inspections are included and DBI confirms the job category.
